subject: compileNimble not working when running in parallel with parLapply and custom distribution

messages.author: f0085bf5ed318bc6
messages.subject: compileNimble not working when running in parallel with parLapply and custom distribution
parts:
Dear List,

I'm trying to run in parallel a code that includes a custom distribution. This works fine when running it normally (i.e. not in parallel), but when I try to implement this using parLapply(), compileNimble() generates the following error message:

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :                                                                                             
  2 nodes produced errors; first error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'rAOR' is not available or its output type is unknown.                        
 This occurred for: eigenBlock(model_theta,1:2,1:6) <<- rAOR(=1,p=model_p[1:6])                   
 This was part of the call:  {                                                                                                                   
  eigenBlock(model_theta,1:2,1:6) <<- rAOR(=1,p=model_p[1:6]) 

Unfortunately, I cannot create a meaningful rAOR() function as dAOR() is used to estimate the log-likelihood of observations with arbitrary errors. Also not sure why this happens only when running in parallel...

The code below replicates the problem with a small mock data. Any help or suggestions are greatly appreciated!!! 

All Best,
Enrico
---
library(nimble)
library(parallel)

# Generate mock data
d  <- list()
d$theta  <- rbind(c(0,0,0.2,0.2,0.6,0),c(0,0.4,0.5,0.1,0,0))
constants <- list()
constants$n.tblocks  <- ncol(d$theta)
constants$weights  <- rep(1,10)
constants$adj  <- c(2,1,3,2,4,3,5,4,6,5)
constants$num <- c(1,2,2,2,2,1)
constants$L  <- length(constants$adj)

# Custom function
dAOR = nimbleFunction(run = function(x=double(2),p=double(1),log=integer(0))
      {
      returnType(double())
      pg = x %*% p
      logProb = sum(log(pg))
      if (log){
      return(logProb)
      } else {
      return(exp(logProb))
      }
      })




# Non Parallel version (working)
icarmodel  <- nimbleCode({
theta[,] ~ dAOR(p=p[1:n.tblocks])
for (i in 1:n.tblocks)
{
p[i] <- lpseq[i]^2 / lpseqSS

}
lpseq[1:n.tblocks] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L],weights[1:L],num[1:n.tblocks],tau,zero_mean = 0)
lpseqSS  <- sum(lpseq[1:n.tblocks]^2)
tau <- 1/sigmap^2
sigmap ~ dexp(1)
})

inits <- list()
inits$sigmap <- 1
inits$lpseq <- rnorm(constants$n.tblocks,0,0.5)
model <- nimbleModel(icarmodel,constants=constants,data=d,inits=inits)
cModel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model)
MCMC <- buildMCMC(conf)
cMCMC <- compileNimble(MCMC)
results <- runMCMC(cMCMC,niter=1000,thin=1,nburnin=500,inits=inits,nchains=2,samplesAsCodaMCMC=T)


#Parallel version (not working)
runFun  <- function(seed,d,constants)
{
library(nimble)
dAOR = nimbleFunction(run = function(x=double(2),p=double(1),log=integer(0))
      {
      returnType(double())
      pg = x %*% p
      logProb = sum(log(pg))
      if (log){
      return(logProb)
      } else {
      return(exp(logProb))
      }
      })

icarmodel  <- nimbleCode({
theta[,] ~ dAOR(p=p[1:n.tblocks])
for (i in 1:n.tblocks)
{
p[i] <- lpseq[i]^2 / lpseqSS

}
lpseq[1:n.tblocks] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L],weights[1:L],num[1:n.tblocks],tau,zero_mean = 0)
lpseqSS  <- sum(lpseq[1:n.tblocks]^2)
tau <- 1/sigmap^2
sigmap ~ dexp(1)
})

inits <- list()
inits$sigmap <- 1
inits$lpseq <- rnorm(constants$n.tblocks,0,0.5)
model <- nimbleModel(icarmodel,constants=constants,data=d,inits=inits)
cModel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model)
MCMC <- buildMCMC(conf)
cMCMC <- compileNimble(MCMC)
results <- runMCMC(cMCMC,niter=1000,thin=1,nburnin=500,inits=inits,samplesAsCodaMCMC=T)
}

cl  <- makeCluster(2)
seeds  <- c(1,2)
out  <- parLapply(cl=cl,X=seeds,fun=runFun,d=d,constants=constants)
stopCluster(cl)

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: compileNimble not working when running in parallel with parLapply and custom distribution
parts:
Hi Enrico,

We have some documentation related to this in our parallelization example, which you may have seen. Specifically toward the end of that example there is some discussion of user-defined distributions. Based on that, you'll need to assign `dAOR` and `rAOR` into the global environment on the workers. The slightly tricky thing in your case is that you are not explicitly defining `rAOR`. It is being defined automatically by NIMBLE in the `nimbleModel()` call.

So if you do the following it should work:
- insert this code after you define dAOR:
assign('dAOR', dAOR, envir = .GlobalEnv)
- insert this code just after the nimbleModel() call
assign('rAOR', rAOR, envir = .GlobalEnv)

(It's also fine to insert both additional lines of code just after the `nimbleModel()` call, but the key thing is only to do the second after `rAOR` is created behind the scenes.

-chris
